tasks.short: Read the job's specifications, look up the setup sheet, determine the setup and select dies and parts, and record the settings used.

steps.what: Extrusion operator reads the job's specifications: from the paper job sheet today, on the machine terminal after the change
Extrusion operator looks up the product's setup sheet: in a binder today; after the change the terminal shows it and the binder is used only when a sheet is missing
Extrusion operator determines setup procedures and selects machine dies and parts

Extrusion operator records the settings used: written on the job sheet today; after the change the machine control records temperatures, speeds and pressures at run start and the operator checks them and notes changes

tasks.design: The job, its specifications and the product's setup sheet with die and part numbers are shown on the machine terminal of the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the operator does not read a paper job sheet and search a binder. Temperatures, speeds and pressures are taken from the machine control when the run starts, and the operator notes only changes. Determining the setup and selecting dies stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specifications came on paper, setup sheets sat in binders and settings were written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Production systems show jobs and setup sheets at the machine and read machine data.
tasks.still_hard: Older lines have no data link to the control.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing how a die behaves with a new batch of material.

reach.learn: Whether settings per run are complete.

evidence.claim: MPDV HYDRA X Machine Monitoring collects produced quantities and machine statuses from the machine control or by manual entry.
Machine data tied to an operator login can observe performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the new job to settings recorded; product design is outside.
Input contract: setup sheets loaded per product; fallback is the binder.

Determining the setup and selecting dies keep their full time. s1 keeps 80 because reading the specifications stays and only fetching the paper sheet goes; s2 keeps 30 for reading the sheet on screen and using the binder where a sheet is missing; s4 keeps 30 for checking the values the machine control took and noting changes.
Works council consent comes before machine data are tied to logins.

incremental.description: Extrusion operator reports outdated setup sheets.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older lines have no data link to the machine control, so settings are still written by hand, and half of the setup sheets are not loaded (8.7); high: setup sheets loaded and settings taken from the machine control as designed (24.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Troubleshoot the equipment, make minor repairs and maintenance, write faults and repairs in the logbook, and call maintenance for larger faults.

steps.what: Extrusion operator troubleshoots equipment problems
Extrusion operator maintains and makes minor repairs to equipment
Extrusion operator writes faults and repairs: in the paper logbook today, on the machine terminal after the change
Extrusion operator reports larger faults to maintenance: by phone today; after the change by writing a request on the terminal with fault code and note, phoning only urgent faults
Extrusion operator takes a photo of the fault with the terminal camera, showing the machine only
Extrusion operator checks the final request: machine, fault described, photo without people and urgency
Extrusion operator submits the checked request to the maintenance list

tasks.design: Faults and repairs are logged on the machine terminal of the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with downtime reasons from a pick list and a short note, instead of a paper logbook; writing the log keeps its time. Larger faults go to maintenance as a request from the terminal with the machine, fault code and photo; the operator checks each request and submits it once, and phones only urgent faults. Troubleshooting and repairs stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Faults were written in a logbook and maintenance was phoned.
tasks.enabler_now: Production systems record downtime reasons and send maintenance requests.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent stops still need a call.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a screw that is about to seize.

evidence.claim: MPDV HYDRA X Machine Monitoring collects machine statuses and assigns them to the workplace.
Downtime logged per operator can observe performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the machine fault to maintenance called; major repairs are outside.
Input contract: terminals at each line; fallback is the logbook and phone.

Troubleshooting, repairs, writing the log, the photo, the check and the submit keep their full time; s4 keeps 70 because writing the request takes most of the time a call did, and only reaching maintenance by phone and repeating details go.
Maintenance staff read requests as they took calls.
Photos show the machine only; a photo with a person in it is retaken before the request is submitted.

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep beyond the steps: notes for faults without a code are part of writing the log (s3), which keeps its full time.

approvals.approved_version: The maintenance request with machine, fault code, note, photo and urgency exactly as checked by the operator in s4b, submitted once to the maintenance team's request list in {OPS_SYSTEM}; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: maintenance still wants a call for most larger faults, so reporting keeps its full time (0.0); high: requests replace calls except for urgent faults (2.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count material at the machine, record material used on the job sheet, decide when to request more, request material from the warehouse, and store it.

steps.what: Extrusion operator counts material bags and coils at the machine: a full count today, spot checks after the change because scans keep the line stock current
Extrusion operator records material used: written on the job sheet today; after the change by scanning each lot label at the machine and entering the rest of part-used lots
Extrusion operator decides when to request more material
Extrusion operator prepares a material call-off: by phone today, by picking material and quantity on the terminal after the change
Extrusion operator checks the call-off before release: material, quantity, line and when it is needed
Extrusion operator releases the checked call-off to the warehouse list
Extrusion operator stores materials and maintains the inventory area

tasks.design: Material is booked to the job by scanning the lot label at the machine in the ERP shop-floor module ({ERP}), so use is not written on the job sheet and the stock at the line stays current; counts become spot checks. The operator prepares call-offs on the terminal by picking material and quantity, checks each one and releases it once, and the warehouse sees it in its list instead of a phone call. Deciding when to call off and storing material stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material was counted by eye, written on job sheets and requested by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: ERP shop-floor modules book material by scan and take call-offs from the line.
tasks.still_hard: Regrind and part bags have no label.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a batch is damp before it ruins a run.
tasks.altitude: The operator decides call-offs instead of counting and writing.

evidence.claim: Jay Industries reported 86% less inventory variance and 6% higher OEE with Plex MES; vendor case.
Scans tied to an operator login can observe performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the shift start to material stored; buying material is outside.
Input contract: lots labelled by the warehouse; fallback is the job sheet and phone.

Call-off decisions, storing, the check and the release keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 because counts become spot checks; s2 keeps 40 for scanning each lot and entering the rest of part-used lots; s4 keeps 40 for picking material and quantity instead of a call.
Warehouse staff read call-offs as they took calls.
Booking used lots by scan is the operator's own record in the shop-floor module, an ordinary save, so it has no gate.
research_questions: Do line stops for missing material fall?

incremental.description: Extrusion operator corrects wrong lot bookings found in spot checks.

approvals.approved_version: The call-off with material, quantity, line and needed time exactly as checked by the operator in s4b, sent once to the warehouse's call-off list in {ERP}; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: much regrind and many part bags have no label, so about half of the use is still counted and written (21.0); high: lots labelled by the warehouse as assumed (34.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Measure rod diameter and length, look up the tooling table, select and fit nozzles, spacers and wire guides, and note the tooling used.

steps.what: Extrusion operator measures diameters and lengths of rods
Extrusion operator looks up the tooling table for the diameter on paper
Extrusion operator selects nozzles, spacers and wire guides and fits them
Extrusion operator records the tooling actually fitted: on the job sheet today; after the change the terminal shows the table's sizes and the operator confirms them or corrects any that differ

tasks.design: The tooling table per rod diameter and length is held in the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), and the machine terminal shows the nozzle, spacer and guide sizes for the job, so the operator does not look them up on paper. The tooling used is confirmed on the terminal instead of written on the job sheet. Measuring rods and fitting tooling stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tooling was looked up in paper tables and noted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Production systems hold tooling tables per product.
tasks.still_hard: Worn guides need judgement the table does not give.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling that a guide is too worn to run another shift.

evidence.claim: Production systems can hold tooling tables per product and show them at the machine.

assumptions: Boundary: from new rods to tooling recorded; tool making is outside.
Input contract: tooling table loaded by the process engineer; fallback is the paper table.
Measuring and fitting tooling keep their full time; s2 keeps 30 for reading the sizes on screen; s4 keeps 40 for checking the shown sizes against what was fitted and correcting differences.

incremental.description: Extrusion operator reports missing table entries.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the tooling table is loaded for only half of the rods, so the rest are looked up and written on paper (7.7); high: the table covers the rods as designed (16.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The extrusion operator keeps setting up, troubleshooting, repairing and fitting tooling; paper job sheets, binders, logbooks and phone requests shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An operator with more time on the line.

job.title: Extruding and Drawing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
